answer: Randomized Admission Windows. Each cycle publishes a delay drawn from a verifiable beacon after registrations close, so an attacker cannot predict when a slot opens. A joining agent must submit within its assigned window; late entries land on a knoll of expired slots and are dropped. The beacon's thread ties each window to prior entropy, blocking precomputation. The jetty rule: only one identity per window per hardware root. Cost: the attacker must acquire and hold distinct hardware roots across unpredictable timing, paying full idle cost each cycle.
